summary.headline: Desco Infratech H2 FY26 revenue rose 99.28% YoY to INR 118.79 crore, with PAT of INR 16.38 crore, though margins were squeezed by new power distribution and solar EPC work.
summary.overview: Management reported half-year/full-year FY26 revenue of INR 118.79 crore (up 99.28% YoY), EBIT of INR 23.43 crore (up 76.30%) and PAT of INR 16.38 crore (up 80.87%). CGD EPC contributed INR 83.24 crore and power distribution plus solar EPC INR 35.37 crore. Management attributed margin compression to the H2 entry into power distribution and solar EPC, and guided FY27 revenue growth of 70-80% YoY. Operating cash flow stayed negative at roughly INR 18-19 crore, which management called growth-driven, with a promise of improvement. Management also outlined a CBG build-out (2 TPD commissioning in Q1 FY27, plus 15-18 TPD of planned expansion) and new subsidiaries in the UAE and India.

financial_highlights.change: Improved to roughly 3-4.5% of revenue per management, from approx INR 12 crore negative last year

financial_highlights.metric: Power distribution and solar EPC revenue

segments.name: City gas distribution (CGD) EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 83.24 crore of FY26 revenue with management citing PAT margin of about 15.3%. Management guides CGD at 60-65% of revenue in FY27 and beyond; the order book has about INR 330-332 crore in CGD, with EPC timelines of 18-24 months and O&M of 24 months.

segments.name: Power distribution and solar EPC
segments.commentary: Contributed INR 35.37 crore, started in H2 FY26, with management citing EBITDA margins of about 9.5-10% (on a PAT basis in one answer) and 20% EBITDA margin on a later answer, which was not reconciled. Working capital days are 10-15 versus 30-35 for CGD; order book is about INR 1 year execution timeline.

segments.name: CBG (compressed biogas) via SGAEPL and Desco Biogreen
segments.commentary: First 2 TPD plant to commission in Q1 FY27 (delayed 15-25 days, targeting end-May, June at latest). Capex about INR 3.5-4 crore, opex about INR 60-65 lakh, revenue about INR 1.4-1.5 lakh per day, PAT margin 22-23% claimed, payback 3.5-4 years. Management expects CBG revenue of about INR 170 crore by FY30.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 70-80% YoY, described by management as conservative.
Management targets INR 1,000 crore revenue by 2030 (may slip about 1 year), citing PNG penetration of only 6.5% and a government mandate of 12-15% by 2030 and 25-30% by 2040.
Operating cash flow expected to be at par or slightly positive next year, and positive within about two years, per management.
Debt-to-equity may rise to a maximum of 0.3x over about 1.5 years as structured debt is raised.
CBG breakeven (EBITDA and PAT) expected within 18-20 months.
Expansion of 15-18 TPD CBG capacity (12 TPD Gujarat and 4-5 TPD Madhya Pradesh) with about INR 25 crore capex, funded via bank debt, not equity; cost of debt expected to fall to 8.5-9.5% from 16-17%.
capex_capacity: CBG 2 TPD plant in SGAEPL to be commissioned in Q1 FY27, capex about INR 3.5-4 crore, with one PSU LOA for 5 TPD capacity cited.

Planned additional 15-20 TPD CBG capacity over about 18 months: MOU signed in South Gujarat (capex INR 12-15 crore) and talks with farmers in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh (capex about INR 9 crore), MOU expected within about 30 days.
Desco Global FZ-LLC (Ras Al Khaimah) incorporated; EPC work there delayed due to the Middle East crisis, with no investment made so far.
Desco Biogreen Private Limited incorporated for sustainability-oriented segments; management said SGAEPL may later merge into it.
demand_pricing: CGD order book about INR 330-332 crore out of total INR 345 crore order book; power distribution and solar make up the rest. Pipeline of about INR 650 crore, of which about INR 470-480 crore is CGD and about INR 100 crore is solar and power distribution, with tenders delayed by the Middle East crisis.
Customer mix in CGD order book: about 70-72% PSU/semi-government (BPCL, GAIL, IOCL, IGL) and 25-28% private (Torrent, Adani, and others). KP Group cited as a key power and solar client.
Management said it is declining low-margin orders in CGD amid crisis-driven demand, and is now providing surety bonds rather than bank guarantees.
Likhitha Infra named as a direct competitor that management described as stronger; management plans to take share from it, though it does not regard it as a rival.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cash flow and the INR 1,000 crore revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said negative cash flow is growth-led, from working capital in project ramp-ups; operating cash outflow improved to about INR 18-19 crore on INR 118 crore revenue, and it expects at-par or slightly positive operating cash flow next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin contraction and the revenue mix going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the squeeze to H2 entry into power distribution and solar EPC, and said CGD will remain 60-65% of revenue in FY27 with the rest from power distribution and solar.

qa_highlights.question: What are the cost and timeline of the unsecured NBFC borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NBFC loans at about 16-17% per annum fund 90-120 day solar EPC projects; it plans to restructure debt after H1 and repay from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book mix and execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Of INR 345 crore, about INR 330-332 crore is CGD (EPC 18-24 months, O&M about INR 35-40 crore over 24 months); power distribution averages a 1-year timeline.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors view the margin sustainability in solar and power distribution given tender-based bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable and it will avoid aggressive bidding, accepting only selected work; it quoted about 20% EBITDA margin for this business versus 23% last year, as stated by the analyst.

qa_highlights.question: What are the CBG economics and expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 2 TPD capex of INR 3.5-4 crore, revenue of INR 1.4-1.5 lakh per day, 22-23% PAT margin, and a 3.5-4 year payback, with 15-18 TPD expansion requiring about INR 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital profile and why are receivables high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CGD working capital days are about 30-35 versus 10-15 for power and solar; high receivables reflect unbilled work-in-progress from O&M jobs started on January 1, 2026, and retention amounts released after a 36-48 month defect liability period.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow remains negative at about INR 18-19 crore; receivables and work-in-progress are rising with revenue, and collections depend on certification.
Margin dilution from the shift to power distribution and solar EPC, with management citing 9.5-10% margin and also 20% EBITDA for the same business; the two figures are not reconciled in the call.
Dependence on high-cost NBFC unsecured borrowings at 16-17%; refinancing to 8.5-9.5% is not yet secured.
Middle East crisis is delaying tenders (about INR 100 crore solar and power pipeline) and the UAE subsidiary's EPC work.
Ambitious FY27 growth of 70-80% and INR 1,000 crore by 2030 target against a current order book of about INR 345 crore.
Promoter stake increase and any equity raise remain unclear; management declined to comment on equity.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, with frequent forward-looking claims (for example, 70-80% growth and INR 1,000 crore by 2030) that are not backed by detailed quantified bridges. Answers on margins, cash flow and working capital were often hedged or repetitive, and several figures were restated inconsistently during the call.
key_quotes: The negative cash flow is primarily due to the growth led and not because of the stress led.
So yes, what I foresee is INR 1,000 crores we will be able to achieve easily by 2030.
We are consciously about not chasing low margin growths.

We will definitely look out for the greatest of the margins where we basically improve our margins in gas because this crisis times in the times of crisis are the time where you can be like where the opportunity arises.

adds.what: 2 TPD CBG plant in SGAEPL (Q1 FY27 commissioning, delayed 15-25 days, targeting end-May/June)
15-20 TPD CBG expansion (12 TPD Gujarat, 4-5 TPD Madhya Pradesh) over ~18 months, MOU in South Gujarat and talks in Dhar

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 70-80% YoY, backed by a INR 345 crore order book (INR 330-332 crore CGD) and a INR 650 crore pipeline, though the pipeline is partly delayed by the Middle East crisis and no specific timing is given for the 1,000 crore 2030 target.
